documents.title: Cedar Shade Loop
documents.text: An easy three kilometer forest loop under tall cedars. Nearly the entire path is shaded, with gentle grades and benches. Families and first time hikers enjoy this quiet walk. Dogs are permitted on leash. There is no reliable drinking water.

documents.title: Sunset Ridge
documents.text: A challenging eight kilometer ridge climb with exposed rocky steps and wide sunset views. The trail gains six hundred meters and offers almost no shade. Bring water and avoid the hottest afternoon hours. Dogs are not permitted.

documents.title: Marsh Boardwalk
documents.text: A flat two kilometer wooden boardwalk crosses a wetland full of birds. The route is wheelchair accessible in dry weather and has observation platforms. It is ideal for a slow wildlife outing. Dogs are not permitted near nesting areas.

documents.title: Fern Falls Path
documents.text: A moderate five kilometer trail follows a cool stream through ferns to a waterfall. Expect muddy sections after rain and several short staircases. The path is shaded for most of its length. Leashed dogs are allowed.

documents.title: Granite Scramble
documents.text: A strenuous six kilometer mountain route crosses boulders and requires hands for several scrambles. The summit gives panoramic views. This trail is unsuitable for children, dogs, or anyone uncomfortable with heights. Carry all water.

documents.title: Meadow Family Walk
documents.text: A one kilometer level walk through open wildflower meadows. Wide packed gravel makes strollers easy to use. Picnic tables sit near the entrance, but the path has little shade. Dogs on leash are welcome.

documents.title: Mirror Lake Circuit
documents.text: A moderate four kilometer circuit around a calm alpine lake. Forest and lakeshore sections alternate, with swimming prohibited to protect habitat. Early mornings bring reflections and bird calls. Dogs are allowed on leash.

documents.title: Echo Canyon
documents.text: A difficult seven kilometer descent into a narrow canyon with steep return switchbacks. Rock walls provide shade but the route can flash flood during storms. No dogs are allowed. The canyon is known for dramatic geology.

documents.title: Pine Access Trail
documents.text: A paved two kilometer route through pine woodland with minimal slope. It is designed for wheelchairs and mobility aids, with frequent rest spots and accessible parking. The trail stays mostly shaded. Service animals are welcome.

documents.title: Orchid Creek
documents.text: An easy three kilometer creekside path passes seasonal orchids and several footbridges. The trail is shaded and good for nature photography. A shallow ford may close after heavy rain. Dogs are allowed on leash.

documents.title: Starwatch Hill
documents.text: A short but steep two kilometer climb to an open hilltop with clear night sky views. There is no lighting, shade, or water. Bring a headlamp for the return. Leashed dogs are allowed.

documents.title: Old Rail Greenway
documents.text: A flat nine kilometer converted railway route with firm gravel and long straight sections. Cyclists and walkers share the path. The trail is accessible at several entrances and has little shade. Dogs on leash are permitted.

documents.title: Moss Gorge
documents.text: A moderate five kilometer woodland route through a cool mossy gorge. Several damp stone steps make it slippery. Small cascades run beside the path. This is a shaded summer option, but dogs are not allowed.

documents.title: Coastal Wind Path
documents.text: An easy four kilometer sea cliff walk with broad ocean views and constant breeze. The path is exposed to sun and wind, with fenced viewpoints. It is not suitable during strong storms. Dogs on leash are welcome.

documents.title: Summit Ladder
documents.text: A very hard ten kilometer ascent using fixed ladders near the summit. The trail gains nine hundred meters and crosses exposed rock. Experienced hikers only. No dogs, bicycles, or young children are permitted.

documents.title: Willow Pond Walk
documents.text: A gentle one kilometer loop around a small pond, with ducks and shaded benches. The surface is smooth and mostly accessible, though one bridge is narrow. Good for a short family outing. Dogs on leash are allowed.

documents.title: Desert Bloom Route
documents.text: A moderate six kilometer dryland route with seasonal cactus flowers and unusual rock formations. It is fully exposed, with no water sources. Start early and carry extra water. Dogs are not recommended because of sharp ground.

documents.title: River Stones Trail
documents.text: A moderate four kilometer riverside hike with multiple shallow stepping stone crossings. Shady trees line much of the river. Crossings become unsafe after rain. Leashed dogs can join when water is low.

documents.title: Birch Autumn Loop
documents.text: An easy five kilometer loop through birch trees that turn gold in autumn. The trail has rolling hills and several rest benches. It is mostly shaded in summer. Dogs on leash are welcome.

documents.title: Eagle View Ridge
documents.text: A hard seven kilometer climb to a high lookout used by soaring eagles. The final ridge is windy and exposed, with a steep drop beside the path. Binoculars are useful. No dogs are allowed.

documents.title: Bamboo Grove Walk
documents.text: A flat three kilometer walk through dense bamboo with deep shade and cool air. The compacted soil path can be muddy after rain. It is a calm beginner route. Leashed dogs are allowed.

documents.title: Volcanic Field
documents.text: A strenuous eight kilometer hike across rough black lava and old crater edges. There is no shade and footing is uneven. Interpretive signs explain the volcanic landscape. Dogs are prohibited due to sharp rock.

documents.title: Maple Picnic Trail
documents.text: An easy two kilometer woodland loop ending at picnic tables beside a small stream. Gentle slopes and shade make it popular with families. The unpaved path is too narrow for wheelchairs. Dogs are welcome on leash.

documents.title: Dune Sunrise Walk
documents.text: A moderate three kilometer walk over soft sand dunes to a sunrise viewpoint. Walking on sand is tiring despite the short distance. There is no shade, so start before dawn and bring water. Dogs are not allowed.

documents.title: Cloud Forest Traverse
documents.text: A demanding nine kilometer high elevation forest traverse. Mist, moss, and bird calls define the route. Weather changes quickly and navigation can be difficult. The trail is shaded, wet, and closed to dogs.

documents.title: Waterfall Viewway
documents.text: A paved one kilometer accessible path reaches a lookout over a waterfall without steep steps. Railings and benches support visitors with limited mobility. The route is shaded. Service animals are permitted.

documents.title: Heather Pass
documents.text: A moderate six kilometer mountain pass trail through flowering heather and open grassland. The climb is steady rather than steep, with far valley views. The route is exposed and can be windy. Leashed dogs are allowed.

documents.title: Otter Bank Trail
documents.text: An easy four kilometer riverbank path with quiet wildlife blinds for watching otters and herons. The route is mostly flat and partly shaded. Keep noise low and leave dogs at home to protect wildlife.

documents.title: Moonlit Garden Circuit
documents.text: A short two kilometer garden circuit with evening opening hours and low path lighting. Smooth paths and benches make it suitable for a relaxed night walk. It is wheelchair accessible. Dogs are not permitted.

documents.title: Redwood Long Trail
documents.text: A moderate twelve kilometer walk among very tall redwood trees. The long distance requires stamina, but elevation change is gentle. Deep forest shade and several streams keep the route cool. Dogs on leash are permitted.
